foreign_a.q: The politician's speech was dismissed as mere ________, lacking any concrete solutions.
foreign_a.why: Ambiguous item — none fits perfectly. 'Ad hoc' (improvised, no long-term plan) is the best of the four.

foreign_a.q: The treaty was signed ________, ensuring privacy away from the media's eyes.
foreign_a.why: In camera = in private.

foreign_a.q: The lawyer filed a petition of ________ to secure the prisoner's release.
foreign_a.why: Writ to bring a detained person before court.

foreign_a.q: His sudden arrival acted as a kind of ________, resolving the narrative too neatly.
foreign_a.why: An unexpected event that neatly resolves a plot.

foreign_a.q: Though she lacked experience, her boss gave her ________ to handle the project independently.
foreign_a.why: Full freedom to act.

foreign_a.q: Philosophers often debate whether morality is relative or whether it exists ________.
foreign_a.why: Known through reason, independent of experience.

foreign_a.q: His biography is widely regarded as his ________, the most important work of his career.
foreign_a.why: One's greatest work.

foreign_a.q: Their romance embodied the spirit of the ________, full of indulgence and pleasure.
foreign_a.why: The sweet life of pleasure.

foreign_a.q: He was known as a ________, constantly prying into others' business.
foreign_a.why: None fits 'prying busybody' (that is 'quidnunc'). Bête noire is the expected pick.

foreign_a.q: The court proceedings emphasized the voice of the people, or the ________.
foreign_a.why: Voice of the people.

foreign_a.q: The rebellion spread rapidly, creating a sense of ________, or lawless confusion.
foreign_a.why: Closest to a rebellion; 'lawless confusion' itself would be anarchy.

foreign_a.q: Despite criticism, he continued to work, convinced that history would prove him ________.
foreign_a.why: Genuine — history would prove him genuine.

foreign_a.q: She justified her decision by saying it was made ________, in the heat of the moment.
foreign_a.why: Made for this moment only, on the spot.

foreign_a.q: The teacher reminded students not to plagiarise, since academic honesty is a matter of ________.
foreign_a.why: Good faith.

foreign_a.q: His alma mater invited him to deliver a convocation speech after two decades.
foreign_a.why: Already filled in on the sheet — one's old school/university.

foreign_a.q: The king ruled with ________, making decisions based only on personal will.
foreign_a.why: Power in practice, not by law. (Laissez-faire = hands-off, the opposite.)

foreign_a.q: The scientist's discovery was published in a journal known for its motto “______” meaning “Truth conquers all.”
foreign_a.why: Truth conquers.

foreign_a.q: During the Renaissance, many thinkers believed in the value of “______,” or the pursuit of knowledge for its own sake.
foreign_a.why: The highest good.

foreign_a.q: He was praised for being a true ________, a citizen of the world.
foreign_a.why: Citizen of the world.

foreign_a.q: The witness testified, but it was clear that he spoke only ________, not the entire truth.
foreign_a.why: In toto = entirely; the sentence says he did NOT speak the entire truth.

foreign_a.q: The law stands firm, regardless of individual opinions, under the doctrine of ________.
foreign_a.why: By law.

foreign_a.q: The general was admired for his ________, or presence of mind during a crisis.
foreign_a.why: Presence of mind, knowing how to act.

foreign_a.q: He accused the journalist of writing ________, a personal attack rather than objective reporting.
foreign_a.why: Attacking the person, not the argument.

foreign_a.q: The debate quickly descended into ________, with both sides refusing to listen.
foreign_a.why: Statements that don't follow — a pointless back-and-forth.

foreign_a.q: Her theory remained merely ________, until supported by empirical evidence.
foreign_a.why: Theoretical, not yet tested by experience.

foreign_a.q: The scholar emphasized the principle of “______,” or the greatest good for the greatest number.
foreign_a.why: Highest/greatest good.

foreign_a.q: The monk lived by the motto “______,” which means “remember you will die.”
foreign_a.why: Remember you will die.

foreign_a.q: The court declared the contract void ________, because it violated fundamental rights.
foreign_a.why: By that very fact.

foreign_a.q: The CEO enjoyed complete authority and often acted as a true ________.
foreign_a.why: Ruler with absolute power.

foreign_a.q: The defence argued that the confession was obtained ________, under duress.
foreign_a.why: Under extreme pressure/duress.
